<!-- Generated by `deltac gen-docs`. Do not edit. -->

Give an assistant [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) (the text below) and ask it to write Delta. Run its program with
`deltac run --json FILE`; the output follows [`/schema/output-v2.json`](/schema/output-v2.json).


Delta is a language whose values are machines, languages, words, grammars and computations.
Run programs at https://delta.nandish.dev/pad/ or with `deltac run --json FILE`.

### Syntax essentials

- One statement per line, or separate with `;`. Comments: `//`, `/* */`.
- Values: ints (64-bit, Euclidean `/` `%`), symbols `'a'`, words `"ab"` (ε = ""), atoms `:q0`,
  sets `{1, 2}`, lists `[1, 2]`, tuples, records `{ from: p }`, maps `{ :q0: 0 }`, functions.
- `let` binds once; `var` can be rebound. `fn f(x) = …` or `fn f(x) { … return … }`.
- Set-builder: `{ e | x ∈ S, cond }`; filter: `{ x ∈ S | cond }`.
- Machines: `dfa M { start q0; accept q1; q0 -a-> q1 }`. Labels: dfa/nfa `a` or `ε`; pda
  `a, X → YZ`; tm `0 → x, R` or `x → R`; mealy `a / 1`; keyword form `read a; pop X; push YZ`.
  Inside `-[ … ]->` an ASCII `->` is allowed. A bare state name is an atom (`M.start == :q0`).
- Options: `dfa M (partial)`, `tm T (missing: error)`, `pda P (accept: by empty-stack)`,
  `pda P (initial stack Z)`.
- Languages: `lang L = { w ∈ {a,b}* | cond }`, `lang R = re"(a ∪ b)* b"`, `lang C = cfg { S -> a S b | ε }`.
  Classes: Finite ⊂ Regular ⊂ DCF ⊂ CF ⊂ CS ⊂ Decidable ⊂ Recognizable ⊂ Any.
- Tests: `check M accepts "w", …`, `check A ≡ B`, `check A ≡ B up to n`, `assert cond`.
- Output: `print a, b`; `show M` (a diagram); `save M to "m.svg"` (.svg .png .pdf .tex .txt .json;
  relative paths only; `deltac` writes the file, the Pad downloads it).
  Undecidable questions (≡ for CF, …) are error E701: use `up to n`.
- Constructions: `explore { alphabet S; start s; step R on a -> e; accept R if c }`,
  `fixpoint X from init { e }`.
- Runs end in accept, reject, loops or unknown: `M.run(w).verdict == :accept`.

### Library

- `to_nfa(R, method: "textbook")`: An NFA for a regular expression. Methods: textbook, thompson, glushkov.
- `to_regex(M, method: "state-elimination", order: [...])`: A regular expression for a finite automaton; `order` sets which states go first. Methods: state-elimination, arden, brzozowski-mccluskey.
- `to_gnfa(M)`: The generalized NFA in special form: new start and accept states, one regex edge between every pair.
- `simplify(R)`: Rewrites a regex with the identities R ∪ ∅ = R, R ε = R, R ∅ = ∅, ∅* = ε, (R*)* = R*.
- `determinize(N)`: The subset construction: a DFA whose states are ε-closed sets of N's states (only reachable sets). Methods: subset.
- `minimize(D, method: "hopcroft")`: The minimal DFA; a state of the result is the set of the states it merges. Methods: hopcroft, moore, brzozowski, table.
- `complete(M)`: Adds a dead state `:dead` for every missing transition.
- `trim(M)`: Keeps only states that are reachable and can reach an accepting state.
- `remove_epsilon(N)`: An NFA without ε-moves for the same language.
- `reverse(M)`: An NFA for the reversed language.
- `complement(M)`: A DFA for the complement (relative to M's alphabet).
- `union(A, B)`: The product DFA accepting when either accepts; states are pairs.
- `intersect(A, B)`: The product DFA accepting when both accept.
- `difference(A, B)`: The product DFA accepting when A accepts and B doesn't.
- `concat(A, B)`: An NFA for the concatenation (ε-edges from A's accepting states).
- `star(A)`: An NFA for the star (a new accepting start state).
- `product(A, B, keep)`: The product DFA accepting where `keep(a_accepts, b_accepts)` is true.
- `equivalent(A, B)`: Whether two languages are equal (decidable for Finite and Regular).
- `subset_of(A, B)`: Whether L(A) ⊆ L(B).
- `pump(D, w)`: The split w = x y z at the first state D's run visits twice: a record {p, x, y, z, state} with |xy| ≤ p, |y| ≥ 1, and x yⁱ z in the language for every i. E504 if w ∉ L(D) or |w| < p.
- `myhill_nerode(D)`: The classes of a regular language: {index, classes, separators}. Each class has its shortest word, whether it is accepting, and (for a dfa) its states; separators maps each pair of class words to the shortest suffix that tells them apart.
- `nullable(G)`: The variables that derive ε.
- `useless(G)`: The variables that derive no word or can't be reached from the start; trim(G) drops them.
- `cnf(G)`: An equivalent grammar in Chomsky normal form (START, DEL, UNIT, TERM, BIN, then trim); steps(cnf(G)) lists each phase.
- `gnf(G)`: An equivalent grammar in Greibach normal form: every rule is A → a B₁…Bₖ (plus S0 → ε if ε ∈ L); new variables Z1, Z2, … remove left recursion.
- `is_ambiguous(G, upto: n)`: A bounded search, not a decision: the first word of length ≤ n with two parse trees. A record {ambiguous, upto, word, trees, note}; the note always states the bound.
- `parse(G, w, method: "earley")`: A parse tree of w (T.root, T.children, T.yield, T.text), or none if w ∉ L(G). CYK parses with cnf(G); steps(T) lists the table cells. Methods: earley, cyk.
- `derive(G, w)`: The sentential forms of a leftmost derivation of w, or none.
- `to_pda(G)`: A pushdown automaton for L(G): states :start, :loop, :accept; the stack holds the rest of a leftmost derivation.
- `to_cfg(P)`: A grammar for a pushdown automaton's language, with variables <p,q> (trimmed).
- `to_single_tape(M)`: A one-tape machine for a deterministic multi-tape one: each cell holds a track per tape with head marks; two sweeps per step. A one-tape machine is returned as it is.
- `mealy_to_moore(M)`: A Moore machine with the same outputs; its states are (q, o).
- `moore_to_mealy(M)`: A Mealy machine whose output is M's without the first λ(q₀).
- `is_empty(L)`: Whether the language is empty (decidable up to CF).
- `is_finite(L)`: Whether the language is finite (decidable up to CF).
- `is_universal(L)`: Whether every word over its alphabet is in it (decidable up to DCF).
- `shortest(L)`: The shortlex-least word of a regular language, or none.
- `words(L, upto: n)`: Every word of a regular language up to length n.
- `count(L, length: n) · count(w, s)`: The number of words of length n in a regular language; or how often symbol s occurs in word w.
- `steps(x)`: The recorded steps of the construction that made x.
- `len(x)`: The length of a word, list, set or map.
- `rev(x)`: A reversed word or list, or the reversed language.
- `prefixes(w) · suffixes(w) · substrings(w)`: The set of prefixes, suffixes or substrings of a word (ε included).
- `power_set(S)`: Every subset of a set (up to 20 elements).
- `set(x) · list(x) · sort(x)`: Converts between collections; sort orders canonically.
- `min(x) · max(x) · sum(x) · abs(n)`: Smallest, largest (canonical order) and sum of a collection; absolute value.
- `keys(m) · values(m) · first(x) · last(x)`: A map's keys (a set) and values (a list); a collection's first and last element.

### Error codes

- E001: Unterminated word or regex. A word "…" or a regex re"…" has no closing quote on its line.
- E002: Unexpected character. A character that isn't part of Delta's syntax.
- E003: Unterminated block comment. A /* comment has no closing */.
- E004: Integer literal too large. int is 64-bit; the literal doesn't fit.
- E005: Bad symbol literal. A symbol is one character, or a name in angle brackets like '<RESET>'.
- E101: Unexpected token. The parser expected something else here; the message says what. Two statements on one line need a `;`.
- E102: Reserved word. `choose`, `import` and `reduce` are reserved for later versions of Delta.
- E103: ASCII arrow inside a bare label. In `-label->` the first `->` ends the edge, so a label containing `->` needs brackets: `-[a, X -> YZ]->`. The quick fix adds them.
- E104: Unbalanced brackets in an edge. A bracketed edge `-[ … ]->` must close with `]->` on the same line, with balanced brackets inside.
- E105: Unterminated edge. An edge starts with `-` but has no `->` before the target state.
- E106: Unknown explore clause. explore takes alphabet, start, step, accept and edges clauses.
- E107: explore without an alphabet. An explore construction needs an `alphabet` clause: the input alphabet of the machine it builds.
- E108: explore without a start. An explore construction needs a `start` clause.
- E109: Bad pattern. `let` binds a name or a tuple of names.
- E110: Expected an expression. Something that isn't an expression appears where a value is needed.
- E201: Unknown name. The name is not defined. The quick fix suggests a close name in scope.
- E202: Rebinding a `let`. `let` binds once; declare the name with `var` to rebind it.
- E203: Assigning an undeclared name. Declare a variable with `var x = …` before assigning to it.
- E204: Argument of the wrong type. The argument doesn't match the parameter's type annotation.
- E205: Infinite set outside lang. Σ* has every word, so it's allowed only inside `lang`. Use Σ^n or Σ^≤n for a finite set.
- E206: Wrong number of arguments. The call passes a different number of arguments than the function takes.
- E207: Calling a model name. Model names start machine literals; conversions are verbs: determinize(N), to_nfa(R), to_gnfa(M).
- E301: Unknown model or property. The model, or one of its properties, doesn't exist.
- E302: No start state. Every machine needs `start q`.
- E303: Undeclared state. With a `states` field, every state used must be declared (this catches typos).
- E304: Symbol not in the alphabet. An edge reads a symbol that isn't in the declared alphabet.
- E305: Nondeterminism in a deterministic model. Two edges from the same state can apply in the same configuration.
- E306: Missing transition in a total model. A dfa needs a move for every state and symbol. Quick fixes: add a dead state, or mark the machine (partial).
- E307: ε-move in a model without epsilon. dfa (and other models without `epsilon`) read a symbol on every edge.
- E308: Missing field in strict mode. `use strict` requires `states` and `alphabet` to be written.
- E309: Bad label. The label doesn't fit the model's label grammar (see Models).
- E312: Unknown option. Machine options are partial, missing: …, accept: by … and initial stack Z.
- E313: Initial stack symbol not in Γ. With a declared stack alphabet, `initial stack Z` must use one of its symbols.
- E401: Regex syntax error. The regex is malformed, for example an unbalanced parenthesis.
- E402: Σ needs an alphabet. Σ in a regex means any symbol; add `over {…}` when the regex has no other symbols.
- E403: Grammar syntax error. Each grammar line is a rule `A -> … | …`.
- E501: Integer overflow. int is 64-bit.
- E502: Division by zero. / and % by 0.
- E503: Index out of range. Indexes start at 0.
- E504: Wrong kind of value. An operation was applied to a value it doesn't take.
- E505: No such member. The record or object has no member with that name.
- E506: Pattern doesn't match. The tuple pattern has a different number of parts.
- E507: Wrong arguments. A call with the wrong number of arguments, or an unknown named argument.
- E508: Not a function. Only functions (and parameterized models) can be called.
- E509: Not available yet. The built-in exists in the language but this version doesn't implement it.
- E512: No transition (missing: error). The machine says a missing transition is an error, and a run reached one.
- E513: rename merges states. M.rename(f) must map different states to different values.
- E514: Unknown file format. save picks the format from the file's extension: .svg, .png, .pdf, .tex, .txt or .json.
- E515: Path leaves the folder. A save path is relative and stays inside the folder the program runs in: no leading /, no drive letter, no `..`.
- E516: Nothing to draw. Only machines can be saved as .svg, .png, .pdf or .tex. Save other values as .txt or .json.
- E517: Not a JFLAP file. In v2.0 `import` reads JFLAP files (.jff) only; modules across Delta files come in v2.1. Without `as`, the file name must be a Delta name: write `import "my file.jff" as M` otherwise.
- E518: File not found. In the terminal, `import` reads the file from the folder the program runs in. In the Pad, open the .jff file first (Files → Open file…); it is then found by its tab name.
- E519: Can't convert the JFLAP file. The file isn't JFLAP XML, or it holds something Delta can't read: Mealy and Moore machines, multi-tape or building-block Turing machines. Finite automata, pushdown automata, one-tape Turing machines and grammars import.
- B601: Step budget reached. The program stopped after the step budget. Outputs so far stay; raise it with budget { steps: … }.
- B602: States budget reached. A construction created more states than the states budget.
- B603: Depth budget reached. Recursion went deeper than the depth budget.
- B604: Output budget reached. The program produced more outputs than the output budget.
- B605: Membership undecided. A run on the word didn't finish within the budget, so membership is unknown.
- E701: Undecidable question. The question is undecidable for the languages' class. The quick fix uses a bounded check: `up to 12`.
- E702: Decidable, not implemented. The question is decidable for this class, but Delta doesn't implement the algorithm (equivalence of DCF languages). Use a bounded check.
- E703: False class claim. `L as c by E`: the evidence disagrees with the language on some word up to length 8.
- W401: Ambiguous + in a regex. Under the default notation `+` means one-or-more. Quick fixes: `a ∪ b` (union) or `a⁺b` (one-or-more).
- X999: Internal error. Something went wrong inside the engine. Your code is kept; please report it.
